name: Lambton Hall (Residence)
summary: An orange-red brick residence trimmed with cream bands, projecting window bays, and a small pedimented blue-green entrance canopy, stepping down from an eight-storey central block to six- and four-storey wings.

evidence.note: Paired punched openings, brick soldier heads, cream bands, and projecting multi-pane window bays flank the entry. Blue-green posts and a split triangular canopy crown. Sunlit red brick sampled #dd987b, lit canopy paint #80b1be.
Tall central range rises behind the blue-green forecourt walkway. Pale masonry continues across the ground floor.
Long low wing with blank stepped end, horizontal light bands and projecting brick bays.
Eight levels at the entrance, paired small windows alternating with projecting grouped windows, canopy on round columns.
Three flat-roofed volumes in a bent arrangement, with a mechanical enclosure at the junction, and entries approached from the courtyard.
P50 17.54 m, P90 25.19 m, maximum 29.05 m above inventory ground. Northwest plateau 17.7 m, long southern plateau 12.0 m, central parapet about 24 m with rooftop plant up to 29.05 m.

notes: Some bedroom windows wrap the corners of shallow projecting bays. The entrance canopy has a split triangular pediment over a lower covered walk. Hidden north-east walls follow the visible residential spacing.
